speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I see you've been experiencing a headache and worsening vision over the last three weeks. To help me understand your condition, can you tell me if the vision changes affect one eye or both, and if the headache is localized to a specific area?

speaker: Patient
text: 69-year-old woman. The patient reports a 3-week history of headache and progressively worsening vision. She has not noticed any other symptoms, including no recent weight changes, no fevers, no night sweats, and no pain elsewhere in the body.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details. Given your age and the progressive nature of your visual changes, is the vision loss in one eye or both? Additionally, do you notice any blurring, shadows, or flashes of light specifically?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Headache. I also have Worsening vision over the past 3 weeks, No weight changes, No fevers, No night sweats, No other pain.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Giant Cell Arteritis (Temporal Arteritis).

I am concerned about the combination of new headache and vision loss in a 69-year-old; have you noticed any scalp tenderness, jaw pain when chewing, or jaw claudication? I also need to know if you have any shoulder or hip stiffness. Please request an urgent ESR and CRP blood test, and we will discuss a temporal artery ultrasound immediately.
